Like the fella says, in Italy for 30 years under the Borgias they had warfare, terror, murder, and bloodshed, but they produced Michelangelo, Leonardo da Vinci, and the Renaissance.
In Switzerland they had brotherly love - they had 500 years of democracy and peace, and what did that produce?
The cuckoo clock.
So long Holly.

I first read John Flavel in paperback editions and then I think back in the 1980's the Banner of Truth published the "Works of John Flavel".
https://heritagebooks.org/products/the-works-of-john-flavel-6-vols.html?srsltid=AfmBOoo0tjW3DVW3VJN9dIALQiU_nx9UocCqgGmwgjNgXCdkg2IRid41 Carol got home from her car appointment around 8:10 AM.
We had devotions and I then left to visit local thrift stores to look for used books to ADD to my used book collection library.
I found these used books today at two local thrift stores-Action House and Southside Goodwill-
"Matrix" A Novel by Lauren Groff "The Woman Who Lost Her Soul" A Novel by Bob Shacochs
"Du Bois on Religion' essays Edited by Phil Zuckerman "The Cold War: A New History" by John Lewis Gaddis "Collected Poems 1934-1952" Poetry by Dylan Thomas "Literary Criticism: A Short History" By William K. Wimsatt, Jr. & Cleanth Brooks "Caliban's Shore: The Wreck of the Grosvenor and the Strange fate of Her Survivors" by Stephen Taylor "Mirrors" Short Stories by Lucy Warner "Constantine and the Bishops: The Politics of Intolerance" Ancient Church History by H.A. Drake This afternoon Amazon delivered a book I had pre-ordered awhile back titled, "Capitalism And Its Critics: A History: From The Industrial Revolution To AI" by John Cassidy.
Carol left around 11 o'clock AM to have lunch and a Bible Study with friends.
She told me after spending time with her friends she plan to go grocery shopping.
Last night before going to bed I read "Foundation Of Joy" by Strickland.
During the evening hours I read primarily, "The Writer's Lot: Culture and Revolution in Eighteenth-Century France" by Robert Darnton and "Free Speech: A History From Socrates To Social Media" by Jacob Mchangama.
I will close to drift.

Neuron:
Simple inversion reflex analog comparator, 0.2s memory per comparison segment.
Layer in a group of three layers (one grain): 1, 3, 12, cross-connected in a radial pattern.
Pass-through buffer to center joining incoming links, pass-through buffer out of center joining outgoing links.
Allow each grain to read and compare specific data segments, filtered on the buffer in; no match, no pass.
Start with 1 grain minimum.

Assign types to grains: sensor, motor, thinker, memory.
Technically memory are sensor neurons with internal feed and feedback.
This assignment can be done randomly on a bias - every zone should have at least one of each, MASTER is always a thinker first, and is connected to a simple clock signal; note that this only changes external connections.
Zones should each have at least one connection to another zone nearby (sourcing from a root provides this initially), and one zone a bit "further" away in the grouping.
Translate information incoming to this artificial brain into analog or analog-like signals, typically through a vocoder.
This should form a minimal, reactive artifical neuron brain capable of self-learning AI response.
